atoms.legal_history: For each of the three profiles, first establish nonzero/valid outputs, then drive rst_n low between two clock edges, observe both between edges and at subsequent edges, and continue after release; for the pass-through instance, also change inputs to confirm that reset does not gate them.

atoms.description: For 4/8, wr_ready combinationally equals rd_ready, and each clock rising edge processes the current 4-bit input only when wr_vld and rd_ready are asserted. For 8/4, the segment advancement condition is likewise wr_vld and rd_ready, not gated by wr_ready: wr_ready is set to 1 on the edge that processes the high half-word, cleared to 0 on the next edge with wr_ready and wr_vld asserted, and otherwise holds, with setting to 1 taking priority. For 8/8, wr_ready=rd_ready, rd_vld=wr_vld. All inputs are stable before the edge; there is no need to interpret this interface as an additional internal FIFO.

atoms.legal_history: The three profiles cover all four wr_vld/rd_ready combinations and continuous valid streams; for 8/4, hold/change inputs to cover both segment positions, wr_ready holding when wr_vld=0, and wr_ready=1 while rd_ready=0.

atoms.description: 4/8 writes two successively processed half-words into rd_data[7:4] and [3:0]; each updated segment remains defined when rd_vld=0. The second segment sets rd_vld, and a newly completed word takes priority over consumption on the same edge. 8/4 alternately takes the high half-word and low half-word from wr_data at that edge and registers the segment into rd_data; each processing edge sets rd_vld, otherwise it holds if the old rd_vld is asserted and ready is not asserted, and clears to 0 in all other cases. rd_data holds on an edge with no processing. For 8/8, rd_data combinationally equals wr_data, adding no latency.

atoms.legal_history: For each profile, input 00, ff, different high and low half-words, bit-by-bit values, and random values; for 4/8, assemble words continuously and check the defined data during the invalid period after the first segment; for 8/4, change wr_data on each edge to confirm that the high and low segments both come from their respective current inputs; for 8/8, change data between edges and observe combinational propagation.

atoms.description: For 4/8, wr_last or wr_align_last returns the position to the first segment after processing this segment, without undoing this segment's write; only a second-segment edge registers wr_last into rd_last, otherwise consuming the old valid value clears rd_last, and it holds in all other cases. A first-segment last is allowed; an incomplete word does not generate valid as a result. 8/4 ignores wr_align_last; when processing the high half-word, rd_last=wr_last, and when processing the low half-word, rd_last=0; when not processing, it holds if the old rd_vld is asserted and ready is not asserted, otherwise it clears to 0. For 8/8, rd_last combinationally equals wr_last, and wr_align_last does not affect outputs.
